interface.title: BioSeq Analyzer
interface.stage_of_work: Early inspection of a single sequence before cloning or annotation: quality check, characterisation and cloning planning
interface.what_it_is_for: Paste or upload one DNA sequence, check that it contains only A/C/G/T, then read its composition, the reverse complement, mRNA and frame +1 translation, six-frame open reading frames above an adjustable length, and a map of 12 common type II restriction sites.

data.note: Used the built-in 'Load example: human insulin mRNA (NM_000207.3)' button: 465 bp, GC 63.87%, longest ORF in frame +3 at 60–392, 110 aa, NcoI at 58, PstI at 240/288/315. Also uploaded the test files insulin_NM_000207.fasta (same results) and invalid_chars_demo.fasta (error: N, R, Y). Pasted three sequences of my own: a string with X/N (rejected), a lowercase 71 bp polylinker with all 10 other enzyme sites (accepted, 'Unnamed sequence'), and a 720 bp GFP coding sequence with a FASTA header (ORF +1, 1–720, 239 aa; NcoI at 169, NdeI at 232). No multi-record FASTA was loaded.

features.name: Sequence input with example loader, FASTA upload and alphabet validation
features.general: Bring in one record by typing, uploading a file or loading a bundled example; the record is checked against the allowed alphabet, and the offending characters are listed before any analysis runs
features.specific: Input method radio (Paste sequence / Upload FASTA file), a DNA sequence textarea that takes plain or FASTA text, the 'Load example: human insulin mRNA' button, and a FASTA uploader (.fasta/.fa/.fna/.txt). A red error 'Found characters that aren't A, C, G or T: N, X' replaces the results. The FASTA header becomes the result title ('Unnamed sequence' otherwise). Lowercase is accepted. (A record picker for multi-sequence FASTA is described in the README but was not exercised.)
steps: choose Paste sequence or Upload FASTA file
load the example, type text or upload a file
press Ctrl+Enter or upload to submit
read the error listing the bad characters, or the titled results
remove the file or edit the text to try again
serves_tasks: Check that the sequence contains only valid bases

features.name: Threshold-filtered six-frame ORF finder
features.general: Scan both strands in all frames for candidate coding regions above a minimum-size slider. Results update live: a summary of the count and best hit, the best hit's product, and a table of all hits with their frame and coordinates. An empty state appears when nothing passes the threshold.
features.specific: 'Minimum protein length (amino acids)' slider (5–300, default 30). Below it: a green 'Found N ORF(s). Longest: frame, position, aa' banner, a 'Protein encoded by the longest ORF' block, and the All ORFs table (Frame, Start, End, Length nt/aa, Protein; minus-strand Start > End). Above all ORFs the banner reads 'No ORFs of at least … found' instead. The table's search, header sort and show/hide columns are the standard Streamlit dataframe toolbar.
steps: open the Open reading frames tab
drag or key the minimum-length slider
read the count, the longest ORF and its protein
read frame and coordinates of each hit in the All ORFs table
optionally search, sort or hide columns with the table toolbar
serves_tasks: Find candidate protein-coding regions on both strands and identify the longest
Search, sort or trim the list of candidate regions (standard table controls)

features.name: Restriction site map with site table and non-cutter list
features.general: Plot where each pattern from a fixed panel occurs along a linear coordinate, one row per pattern, with hover details, paired with a per-pattern table of positions and a list of patterns that never occur
features.specific: Restriction sites tab: a Restriction map tick chart over 'Position in sequence (bp)' with one row per cutting enzyme (hover shows Enzyme and Position). Below it is a table of Enzyme, Recognition site, Number of sites and Positions, and a 'Non-cutters (no site in this sequence)' line across the 12-enzyme panel. Show data, Download as PNG, Copy Vega-Lite spec and Fullscreen come from the standard Vega chart toolbar.

not_done: Download as CSV on the All ORFs and restriction tables: the button was pressed twice but no file appeared in downloads, probably because it needs a browser save dialog that the headless browser cannot answer. The table export is untested.
The first 'Copy to clipboard' attempt on the reverse complement left the clipboard empty (screens/012.webp). A later attempt worked (screens/045.webp).
The restriction map does not respond to the zoom wheel (Ctrl+scroll just scrolled the page, screens/028.webp), so the map cannot be zoomed or panned.
Comparing site positions with the README's annotated C-peptide region was not done: the interface has no annotation track. Only the overlap with the ORF coordinates was read (task n1).
Switching the input method clears the pasted text (screens/046.webp), and the ORF slider resets to 30 when new data loads, so settings do not carry over between inputs.

Task n1 was added in review and has no replay.
